headline: Markets claw back losses as rate-cut odds climb again
body: Equities extended their recovery into the new week, with the Nasdaq posting one of its stronger single-session gains of the month as traders kept buying the dip that followed a rough stretch earlier in November. The S&P 500 had slid for five consecutive sessions in mid-November, falling to roughly 6% below its early-October record high as worries about AI capital spending and financing pushed volatility to its highest level since the spring tariff scare. That drawdown has since stabilized, and the latest session's bounce came alongside firming bets that the Federal Reserve will cut rates again at its December meeting — a shift in futures-implied odds that gave risk assets a tailwind even as the underlying debate over AI-related debt and profitability timelines remains unresolved.

Retail and social-media chatter didn't offer a sharp, confirmable signal specific to today, so this read leans more on price action and macro headlines than on a fresh wave of trader sentiment. Recent commentary has described retail positioning on names like SPY and QQQ as leaning cautious to bearish even as the tape recovers, a disconnect consistent with a market climbing back more on relief and rate-cut hope than on renewed conviction. Put together, the setup looks like a tentative unwind of extreme-fear positioning rather than a full return to risk-on euphoria — participants willing to re-engage on dips while still watching how the AI-financing story and next month's Fed decision play out.
